newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMB says sees satisfactory 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: AMB says sees satisfactory 1996 profits.

text.p: German insurer Aaachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs AG (AMB) said on Friday its expected satisfactory growth and earnings in the current year, after net profit rose some 30 percent in 1996.

In a mandatory statement, AMB said: "The group expects satisfactory growth overall for the current year...If capital markets develop favourably one could expect that the group net profit will be satisfactory again."
AMB reported group net profit of around 340 million marks ($200.7 million) for 1996, around 30 percent up from the previous year and said its earnings per share should also show strong growth.
Profit growth in 1996 was primarily driven by successful restructuring measures and high profits at foreign units, particularly in the Netherlands, AMB said.
Total group sales reached just under 20 billion marks, a rise of 6.5 percent, of which insurance accounted for 17 billion marks, up from 16.2 billion the previous year.
AMB said its life insurance business had developed especially well, with premium income up to 9.3 billion marks from 8.8 billion, better than the market average.
German premiums rose 4.4 percent while foreign premiums rose 9.7 percent, to which AMB said its Dutch units had contributed most.
The group's mortgage business, its Badenia Bausparkasse unit, extended its market share in 1996 and is also expected to improve its profits, AMB said.
Badenia's net new business rose more than 31 percent to nearly 8.2 billion marks.
